faults.description: Rubber seal at the bottom of the door is torn, leaving about a 1 inch gap to the outside.
faults.hint: Where could something small get in?
faults.learningNote: Small gaps are an easy entry route for pests.

faults.description: Heavy weed growth against the building.
faults.learningNote: Plants give pests cover and a way in.

faults.description: Mouse droppings in a dark corner behind a pallet of salt.
faults.learningNote: Evidence of pests in the ingredient store. Stock that never moves hides activity. Consider critical if on or near product.

faults.description: Dusty bait station with an out-of-date inspection sticker.
faults.hint: Is the pest monitoring up to date?
faults.learningNote: The pest monitoring is not being done as planned.

faults.description: Pallet of salt not moved for about six months and out of date.
faults.learningNote: Old stock is not being rotated and gives pests somewhere to hide.

faults.description: Leaking overhead pipe "repaired" with duct tape, a bucket catching drips, and drips reaching a surface that touches product.
faults.learningNote: A temporary fix is being used instead of a proper repair, with a risk of contamination.
